newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish opposition says Yates should be sacked.
newsitem.headline: Irish opposition says Yates should be sacked.

text.p: Irish agriculture minister Ivan Yates should be sacked for his handling of the recent Russian ban on beef from three Irish counties, opposition leader Bertie Ahern told parliament on Thursday.

Ireland signed a deal last week stopping exports from three counties to Russia because of Russian fears about mad cow disease. Yates said he was forced to agree to the deal because Russia had threatened to ban all Irish beef.
Opposition parties on Thursday accused Yates of deliberately misleading the public over the circumstances of the deal's signing.
They said he had implied he signed it personally at Dublin airport, when in fact he was not at the airport and officials signed it on his behalf.

Ahern asked Yates in parliament if he had agreed to the ban "on an ultimatum from three Russian vets over the telephone". He wanted to know where Yates was during the negotiations and who he had consulted.
"An inexperienced minister does not make these kind of decisions on his own without the prime minister's knowledge and backing. If he did, he should be sacked," Ahern said.
